skill.name: rdkit
skill.description: Use RDKit for cheminformatics workflows including molecular parsing, descriptor calculation, fingerprints, similarity search, SMARTS filtering, reactions, coordinate generation, and visualization.
skill.summary: Analyze molecules, descriptors, fingerprints, substructures, reactions, and visualizations with RDKit.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static shell, reconnaissance, sensitive-key, filesystem, and obfuscation hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, RDKit SMARTS syntax, dictionary keys(), and expected local outputs. The bundled scripts only write files when a user supplies output arguments. One medium semantic issue remains because the documentation shows pickle loading without a trusted-file warning.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the pickle loading example with SDF or SMILES storage, or warn users to only load pickle files from trusted sources.
Add overwrite checks or a force flag before writing CSV, SDF, SMILES, image, or report outputs.

semantic_findings.description: The documentation shows storing molecules with pickle and loading them with pickle.load without warning users to trust the file source. Loading untrusted pickle data can execute attacker-controlled code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The pickle.load example is explicit and lacks a trusted-data warning. The risk is limited because it is documentation, not code that executes automatically.

content.value_statement: Cheminformatics work often requires precise molecular parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, and substructure logic. This skill provides RDKit guidance and reusable scripts for research workflows.
actual_capabilities: Parse SMILES, SDF, MOL, and InChI molecules with RDKit examples.
Calculate molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen bonding, ring, and drug-likeness descriptors.
Generate Morgan, RDKit, MACCS, atom-pair, and torsion fingerprints for similarity search.
Filter molecule sets with SMARTS patterns and built-in functional group libraries.
Create 2D and 3D coordinates, conformers, alignments, and molecule images.
Use bundled scripts for property tables, similarity hits, and substructure filtering reports.
limitations: RDKit must be installed in the runtime environment before examples or scripts can run.
The skill does not validate scientific conclusions or replace expert chemistry review.
Large molecule libraries may need memory and performance tuning outside the examples.
Some descriptor and 3D methods depend on valid sanitization and appropriate molecular inputs.

use_cases.title: Screen Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Run fingerprint similarity searches and substructure filters across SMILES or SDF files.

use_cases.title: Prepare Molecular Features
use_cases.description: Generate descriptors and fingerprints for modeling, clustering, or quality control workflows.

use_cases.title: Inspect Chemical Structures
use_cases.description: Create visual depictions, highlight substructures, and troubleshoot sanitization issues.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Basic Properties
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the RDKit skill to calculate molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, and Lipinski status for these SMILES: [paste molecules].

prompt_templates.title: Find Similar Compounds
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RDKit Morgan fingerprints to compare this query molecule against my SMILES file and explain the highest similarity hits.

prompt_templates.title: Filter By SMARTS
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a SMARTS filtering plan that includes aromatic amines, excludes acyl chlorides, and reports which molecules matched each pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an RDKit workflow for sanitizing molecules, generating descriptors, clustering by fingerprints, and exporting reviewer-ready summaries.

output_examples.input: SMILES list for aspirin, caffeine, and ethanol.
output_examples.output: A descriptor summary with formula, molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen bond counts, and Lipinski pass status.

output_examples.input: A benzene query molecule and a compound library file.
output_examples.output: A ranked similarity hit list with compound names, canonical SMILES, and Tanimoto scores.

output_examples.input: A molecule file and SMARTS patterns for PAINS and reactive groups.
output_examples.output: A filtering summary that separates included, excluded, and unmatched molecules with matched pattern names.

best_practices: Check every molecule for parse failures before calculating descriptors or fingerprints.
Use explicit sanitization handling when working with unusual valence, salts, or radicals.
Choose fingerprint methods and similarity thresholds that match the scientific question.
anti_patterns: Do not treat descriptor values as biological activity without validation data.
Do not load pickle files from untrusted sources.
Do not reuse SMARTS filters without confirming they match the intended chemistry.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use RDKit for molecular analysis, search, filtering, reactions, and visualization.

faq.question: Does it install RDKit?
faq.answer: No. RDKit must already be installed with a supported Python environment.

faq.question: Can it process SDF and SMILES files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and scripts cover SDF, MOL, SMILES, and text molecule inputs.

faq.question: Can it generate molecular images?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents RDKit drawing utilities for single molecules, grids, highlighted atoms, and fingerprint bits.

faq.question: Is it suitable for drug discovery work?
faq.answer: Yes, for computational support tasks such as descriptors, filters, fingerprints, and similarity analysis.

faq.question: What should users be careful about?
faq.answer: Users should validate molecules, avoid untrusted pickle files, and review chemical assumptions with domain experts.
